turkey_specific_content:
Very little real Turkey-specific content. The topic is universal Western tropical astrology. Items to adapt:
(1) l.202 says the date ranges in the table are 'commonly used in Turkey'. The ranges themselves (Aries Mar 21–Apr 19 … Pisces Feb 19–Mar 20) match the standard Western ranges used by astrology.com and others, so keep the dates and reword this as 'the commonly used tropical-zodiac dates'.
(2) Turkish sign names are used as object keys in BURCLAR (l.249-296) and shown directly via #s-ad (l.396) and the share text (l.411). Rename the keys to Aries…Pisces; the Object.entries iteration order sets the tie-break, so keep the same order. Translate elmod values ('Ateş · Öncü' → 'Fire · Cardinal'), the anahtar keywords, yorum, isik and the 10 questions with 40 options. Leave the internal codes ates/toprak/hava/su and oncu/sabit/degisken untouched, because scoring depends on them.
(3) Table vocabulary: Element / Modality (Öncü = Cardinal, Sabit = Fixed, Değişken = Mutable) / Ruling planet. lib/mcp-dil.js already maps sign and planet names TR→EN.
(4) All internal links point to Turkish pages: koc-burcu.html…balik-burcu.html (l.206-217), dogum-haritasi-hesaplama.html (l.221), yukselen-burc-nedir.html, ay-burcu-nedir.html (l.223), burclar.html, gunes-ay-yukselen.html, uyum-testi.html (l.227-229). On EN, link only to EN pages that exist in phase 1 (e.g. an EN birth chart or rising sign tool if built) and drop the rest. The sign names in the table become plain text.
(5) The cookie banner (l.437) cites 'Gizlilik & KVKK', which is Turkish data-protection law. EN needs an English privacy notice (GDPR-style wording) and an EN privacy page link.
(6) Login/Hesabım swap script (l.159) and the Giriş link: the Supabase account area is Turkish only, so remove both on EN.
(7) The share text and title (l.411, 414) and toasts (l.418, 420) need English; the share URL is hardcoded to /hangi-burcsun.html and must point to the EN slug.
(8) <html lang="tr"> becomes en; add hreflang tr/en/x-default pairs and an EN canonical.

rationale:
Technically this is about the easiest page on the site to put into English. There is no backend call: the quiz is pure client-side JS. That code is roughly 140 Turkish strings (about 650 words): 12 sign names, 12 element/modality labels, 36 keywords, 12 descriptions, 12 'light side' lines, 10 questions with 40 answers, a 'Soru x / y' counter, the share text and 2 toasts. There's also about 315 words of static info section and about 40 words of hero, intro and buttons. Everything sits in plain data objects, so translation won't break the logic as long as the el/mod codes stay unchanged. The content is universal, and the zodiac dates already match the Western standard. The only shared-script work is an English menu that skips asterna-widget.js and pwa.js. That work is shared by every EN page anyway.

The case against phase 1 is commercial. Unique value and ranking odds are low. 'Which zodiac sign are you quiz' and 'what zodiac sign am I' have real English demand. But BuzzFeed, Cosmopolitan, Playbuzz-style quiz sites, astrology.com and dozens of quiz farms dominate those results. 'Zodiac sign dates' is owned by astrology.com, Cafe Astrology, Allure, Wikipedia and similar sites. A generic 10-question quiz on a new /en/ subfolder with Turkish domain authority is very unlikely to rank. Its main upside is social sharing (navigator.share) and being an entry point that links to EN tools. On top of that, most of its internal links (12 sign pages, rising and moon sign explainers, compatibility) would be dead on EN unless those pages are also built.

Recommendation: leave it out of the core phase 1, which should go to client-side calculators with distinctive output (birth chart, rising or moon sign and so on, if their backends allow English output). Use it as a cheap filler or early phase 2 page. If it does go in, add a client-side birth-date sign finder (a trivial date→sign lookup) so it also targets 'what is my zodiac sign' and 'zodiac sign calculator'. Estimated effort is 1–2 hours.

Minor notes for the translator. Question 8 (l.336) has two water answers and no earth answer, and question 9 (l.341) has two earth answers and no water answer. Ties go to whichever sign comes first in object order (Aries). Both are harmless but worth knowing.
